item.title: What to Know About the Bomb Threats Disrupting Flights in Europe
item.description:
AdvertisementSKIP ADVERTISEMENTYou have a preview view of this article while we are checking your access. When we have confirmed access, the full article content will load.
Bomb threats targeted several European airlines on Thursday, disrupting more than a dozen flights in Italy, France and elsewhere after a series of similar threats this week upended travel for some across the region.
All the planes targeted this week have landed safely, some escorted by fighter jets, and no explosives have been found on any of them, according to officials. The sources of the threats were not clear.
Anxiety over airspace security is running high in Europe. A spate of hybrid warfare attacks and intimidation tactics have rattled air travel in recent months as Russia’s war against Ukraine spills over its borders.
Here’s what we know:
What flights were affected on Thursday?
In Italy, a Finnair plane from Helsinki was escorted to an airport in Rome by military jets after a threat, officials said. French officials said that an Aer Lingus plane flying to Rome from Dublin had been diverted to an air base in France because of a threat. The authorities in the Czech Republic said that four planes heading to Prague had received bomb threats.
Three Ryanair flights bound for Sofia, Bulgaria, from Copenhagen, Madrid and London were also threatened, the Bulgarian transport ministry said in a statement. The flights from Madrid and Copenhagen landed at Sofia Airport; the flight from London was diverted to an airport in Plovdiv, a city in southern Bulgaria. Bulgaria’s defense ministry said that its air force had escorted the three flights with fighter jets.
Two LOT Polish Airlines flights were also targeted, the company said. A flight that was headed to Paris was stopped while taxiing before it was searched and cleared, and a flight on its way to Brussels from Warsaw was also cleared after security inspections in the air and on the ground.
